name: Blockchain & Smart Contract Security
description: Security of blockchains, consensus, cryptocurrencies, DeFi, and smart contracts.
narrative:
The earliest work on this list (2018) attacks blockchain security on two fronts that would define the field. The first front is making smart contracts safe to deploy: automated analysis tools arrived almost simultaneously, with ZEUS: Analyzing Safety of Smart Contracts (NDSS 2018) and Securify: Practical Security Analysis of Smart Contracts (CCS 2018) bringing formal verification and symbolic reasoning to Ethereum, while teEther: Gnawing at Ethereum to Automatically Exploit Smart Contracts (USENIX 2018) showed the attacker's side by generating exploits automatically. The second front is scalability of the underlying ledger, where OmniLedger (S&P 2018) and RapidChain (CCS 2018) used sharding, and BEAT: Asynchronous BFT Made Practical (CCS 2018) pushed consensus forward. Cryptographic plumbing matured in parallel, most visibly with Bulletproofs (S&P 2018), whose short, trustless-setup zero-knowledge proofs became foundational for confidential transactions far beyond cryptocurrency.

Around 2019 the field broadened from "can we secure one chain" to building a usable layered ecosystem. Payment and state channels became a serious research thread (General State Channel Networks, CCS 2018; Perun, S&P 2019; Anonymous Multi-Hop Locks, NDSS 2019), and cross-chain interoperability emerged with XCLAIM (S&P 2019) and Proof-of-Stake Sidechains (S&P 2019). Smart-contract analysis kept advancing toward hybrid techniques, as in Learning to Fuzz from Symbolic Execution (CCS 2019), while empirical security studies like The Art of The Scam: Demystifying Honeypots (USENIX 2019) started measuring real-world abuse rather than just hypothetical bugs. Threshold ECDSA work (S&P 2019, building on CCS 2018) addressed how to custody keys safely.

The decisive conceptual shift comes with Flash Boys 2.0 (S&P 2020), which named miner/blockchain extractable value (MEV) and reframed frontrunning and consensus instability as a first-class economic-security problem. This opened a wave of DeFi-security research: High-Frequency Trading on Decentralized On-Chain Exchanges (S&P 2021), the empirical Frontrunner Jones (USENIX 2021), and Quantifying Blockchain Extractable Value: How dark is the forest? (S&P 2022) measured the scale of the threat. Verification kept pace through VerX (S&P 2020), and consensus advanced via Sync HotStuff (S&P 2020) and DAG-based Bullshark (CCS 2022). Bridging trusted off-chain and on-chain worlds matured with DECO (CCS 2020) and zkBridge (CCS 2022).

Today the area has consolidated around the financial layer it created. Attention has moved to the security of whole application ecosystems, with Understanding Security Issues in the NFT Ecosystem (CCS 2022) and the synthesizing SoK: Decentralized Finance (DeFi) Attacks (S&P 2023), which catalogs the now-mature taxonomy of how value is stolen on-chain. The throughline across these venues is a steady move from proving individual contracts correct, to scaling and connecting chains, to confronting the adversarial economics that emerge once real money flows through them.

milestones.title: Bulletproofs: Short Proofs for Confidential Transactions and More
milestones.note: introduced short, trustless-setup zero-knowledge range proofs that became foundational cryptographic infrastructure for confidential transactions

milestones.title: Securify: Practical Security Analysis of Smart Contracts
milestones.note: established practical automated static analysis as a defense for vulnerable smart contracts

milestones.title: OmniLedger: A Secure, Scale-Out, Decentralized Ledger via Sharding
milestones.note: showed sharding could scale a permissionless ledger toward payment-processor throughput without sacrificing security

milestones.title: Perun: Virtual Payment Hubs over Cryptocurrencies
milestones.note: advanced off-chain payment/state channels as a scalable layer-2 approach to cheap micropayments

milestones.title: Flash Boys 2.0: Frontrunning in Decentralized Exchanges, Miner Extractable Value, and Consensus Instability
milestones.note: named miner-extractable value and reframed DeFi frontrunning as a first-class economic-security and consensus threat

milestones.title: DECO: Liberating Web Data Using Decentralized Oracles for TLS
milestones.note: made trustworthy off-chain-to-on-chain data oracles practical, bridging real web data into smart contracts

milestones.title: Quantifying Blockchain Extractable Value: How dark is the forest?
milestones.note: empirically quantified the scale of extractable value, grounding the MEV threat in measured reality

milestones.title: SoK: Decentralized Finance (DeFi) Attacks
milestones.note: systematized the mature taxonomy of DeFi attacks, marking the field's consolidation around financial-layer security
